    <div class="abstract__body"><img class="abstract__portrait" src="{{ '/assets/img/perez.jpeg' | relative_url }}" alt="">{% capture abstract_md %}[Fernando Pérez](https://fernandoperez.org) is an Associate Professor in Statistics at UC Berkeley, Faculty Scientist at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, faculty director of the Berkeley Institute for Data Science ([BIDS](https://bids.berkeley.edu)), and co-director of the Eric and Wendy Schmidt Center for Data Science &amp; Environment ([DSE](https://dse.berkeley.edu)). His research focuses on the intersection of interactive computing, open science, and AI-based tools for science, with a particular focus on questions related to the earth's cryosphere, climate change and environmental sustainability. He also co-leads [the JupyterHealth initiative that bring open source and AI into healthcare](http://jupyterhealth.org), in partnership with clinical and biomedical researchers. He created IPython while a graduate student in 2001 and co-founded its successor, [Project Jupyter](https://jupyter.org). At Berkeley, he also leads computing platforms at the Bakar Institute for Digital Materials for the Planet ([BIDMaP](https://bidmap.berkeley.edu)). Also an entrepreneur, he is a co-founder and CTO of [AIMATX](https://aimatx.ai), which uses AI tools to accelerate the discovery of novel materials for the economy of the future.

Fernando regularly lectures about scientific computing, data science and open science. He co-founded the International Interactive Computing Collaboration ([2i2c](https://2i2c.org)) to provide open infrastructure for modern science and education, and is also a founding member of [NumFOCUS](https://numfocus.org). He is the recipient of the 2024 Exceptional Public Service Medal from NASA, the 2024 "Champions of Open Science" recognition from the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, the 2017 ACM Software Systems Award and the 2012 Award for the Advancement of Free Software from the Free Software Foundation. He is a Kavli Frontiers Fellow of the US National Academy of Sciences (2016). Fernando holds a PhD in particle physics from the University of Colorado at Boulder, which he followed with postdoctoral research in applied mathematics.{% endcapture %}{{ abstract_md | markdownify }}</div>
